svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: The same participant-safe task and benchmark-owned concurrent initial workstreams enter independent Linear and Async routes. A, B and C are illustrative workstreams with different execution extents, not fixed event themes, outcomes or required identities. Linear waits for all terminal child states and shows one stable atomic batch before main integration. Async shows main and children overlapping in time. A shared running-group boundary supplies Events: real terminal notifications and supported evaluator/runtime events, not only successful results. Evaluator-private Scenario control uses the case rules from Task setup. Hold, Trigger and Release summarize event policy: events can pass immediately, be staged until case-defined runtime or prior-event conditions, or be replayed as supported; timeout, crash and pressure events can arise at runtime boundaries. This is not a mandatory delayed-success pipeline or a fixed provisional-draft trigger. Policy-specific bounded waiting and fallback remain applicable. Public submission validation stays distinct from private checks. The solid event path reaches actual inclusion in a launched main-model request and starts the response, without preempting an in-flight main API call. Main can replan affected work and keep valid work within the same event, and may issue supported group management actions. The dashed Control interface targets the group rather than any fixed child; it does not imply hot task mutation, automatic replacement, or one required action per event theme. Plain child document glyphs do not assert successful or correct results. All timeline extents are qualitative and unmeasured. Run records cover the entire execution and event-boundary evidence. BTS denotes eventual whole-run final states. Independent DRS uses half process plus half event outcome, without strict attribution to the displayed response fragment. Metrics separately aggregate through repetitions and tasks to equal-weight event-theme means with coverage reported independently.
